learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the principles of sustainable development, explore the importance of green jobs, and learn how to protect our environment for future generations!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs—balancing economic growth, social inclusion, and environmental protection.
A set of 17 global goals established by the United Nations in 2015 to end poverty, protect the planet, and ensure peace and prosperity for all by 2030 (e.g., Clean Water, Climate Action).
Green jobs are careers in agriculture, manufacturing, energy, or design that help preserve or restore the environment (like solar panel technicians, organic farmers, and waste recycling managers).
Practicing the 4 Rs (Refuse, Reduce, Reuse, Recycle), conserving water and electricity, using public transport, and adopting eco-friendly daily habits.

fun_activity.title: ♻️ The Waste Audit
fun_activity.instructions: Look inside your home dustbin today. Identify one item that was thrown away but could have been Reused or Recycled instead (like a plastic jar or cardboard box). Plan how to reuse it next time!

exam_tips: 📌 Memorize the definition of Sustainable Development given by the Brundtland Commission.
📌 Know at least 4 examples of 'Green Jobs' across different sectors (e.g., Solar installer, E-waste recycler, Green building architect, Organic farmer).
📌 Explain the importance of transitioning from non-renewable fossil fuels to renewable energy sources.
quick_recap: ⭐ There are 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) adopted by all UN Member States.
⭐ Organic farming protects soil health and prevents toxic chemical runoff into water bodies.
⭐ Green skills are technical skills, knowledge, and values needed to work in environmentally sustainable jobs.
